title: Every VTCStreamEnable is refused: the handler deserializes a tagged enum from a body with no @type
design:
FOUND 2026-11-25 by bead mimid-1wgh.114.10's test, which is its
regression test.

WHAT HAPPENED. A client opening /jmap/ws and sending the correct frame

    {"@type": "VTCStreamEnable"}

got back

    {"@type":"RequestError","status":400,
     "type":"urn:ietf:params:jmap:error:notRequest",
     "detail":"Malformed VTCStreamEnable: missing field `@type`"}

so no subscription was ever enabled and no call signal was ever
delivered, to anyone, ever.

THE MECHANISM. crates/mimid-agent-jmap/src/vtc_stream.rs's
ExtensionHandler::handle did

    match message.deserialize::<VtcStreamMessage>()? { ... }

jmap-websocket's ExtensionMessage documents `body` as "Every member of
the message except `@type`", and `deserialize` deserializes that body.
VtcStreamMessage is internally tagged on `@type`. So the tag is removed
by the transport and then required by the type: the call could not
succeed for any input. The error text even says so, and nothing read it.

WHY NO TEST CAUGHT IT. vtc_stream.rs's three unit tests cover
`candidate_of`, the SDP-fragment decoder, and nothing else. Nothing
opened a socket. The handler compiled, linted and looked right.

THE FIX. Dispatch on `message.message_type`, which is what the transport
already routed on (`message_types()`), and deserialize the one frame
type: VtcStreamEnable for "VTCStreamEnable", reset for
"VTCStreamDisable". ENABLE and DISABLE become named constants so the
list the transport is given and the arms that handle it cannot drift.

LESSON WORTH KEEPING: `deserialize::<T>()` on an ExtensionMessage must be
the INNER frame type, never the tagged envelope. Any other extension
handler mimid adds has the same trap waiting.
close_reason: Fixed in the commit above; the regression test is tests/vtc_negotiation.rs (bead mimid-1wgh.114.10), which failed on each of the three in turn.
